title: Tensor pullback on commuting scheme-chart triangles
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with structure rings and module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $V\to Y$ be an etale scheme chart and $q=(U\to X,U\to V)$ a commuting chart triangle in $\mathcal A(f,V)$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. On both localized sites $Y_{\mathrm{et}}/V$ and $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], additive sheafification exists in the original section universe and preserves finite limits. There exists a functor $F_q:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y|_V)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X|_U)$ that is left adjoint, an isomorphism $\mathcal O_X|_U\simeq F_q(\mathcal O_Y|_V)$, and a natural isomorphism $F_q(M|_V)\simeq(f^*M)|_U$ for every module sheaf $M$ on $Y$. Here restriction is the canonical slice restriction, and $f^*$ is exactly the left adjoint of the specified chart-limit direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. No quasi-coherence of $M$, flatness of $f$, or covering property of $U$ or $V$ is assumed.

proof.text: The localized small etale site over a scheme chart V is the small etale site of V: retain the scheme map to V, or compose it with V to Y. These inverse equivalences preserve coverings and the regular-function ring. The affine etale basis has a small skeleton in the section universe, so the usual left exact additive sheafification on the scheme small etale site transports to the slice. Apply the same argument to U. This is the stronger sheafification fact constructed internally in the existing small-site slice proof.

source.place: Tag 04J0 (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites); spaces-properties.tex Tags 03G1, 03ED. The scheme sheafification instance is Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.AffineEtale, lines 105-114.

proof.text: Pass to enlarged etale ringed sites. Localize the base-change morphism at V, and then restrict along the enlarged arrow U to X times_Y V supplied by q. The base-change functor preserves finite limits and covers; its slice functor is continuous. The module adjunction supplies tensor pullback on the localized ringed sites. Compose this pullback with the etale source restriction and transport through the ringed scheme-object equivalences to get F_q. All factors are left adjoints.

Tensor pullback sends the source structure module A to the target structure module B. The maps b tensor a to b times the image of a and b to b tensor 1 are mutually inverse, by the balancing relation. These are compatible with restriction, so sheafification gives the same inverse maps. The ringed equivalences and etale restriction preserve the structure rings. Their composite is the asserted structure-module isomorphism.

The localization comparison identifies F_q applied to the restriction of M with the restriction of enlarged tensor pullback. The chart-limit/enlarged-sections comparison identifies the direct image of this global tensor pullback with the specified moduleDirectImage f. Uniqueness of left adjoints then identifies this tensor pullback with moduleTensorPullback f. Compose the two comparisons to obtain the required natural isomorphism for every M.

theorem moduleTensorPullback_chart_functor {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (V : Y.EtaleSite)
    (q : ModuleChart f V) :
    HasSheafify (Y.etaleTopology.over V) AddCommGrpCat.{u} ∧
      HasSheafify (X.etaleTopology.over q.left) AddCommGrpCat.{u} ∧
      ∃ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Y.structureSheaf.over V) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (X.structureSheaf.over q.left),
      F.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
      Nonempty (SheafOfModules.unit (X.structureSheaf.over q.left) ≅
        F.obj (SheafOfModules.unit (Y.structureSheaf.over V))) ∧
      Nonempty (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.structureSheaf V ⋙ F ≅
        moduleTensorPullback f ⋙ SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.structureSheaf q.left)
